'''Lal Bahadur Shastri Airport''' {{Airport codes|VNS|VEBN}} is an [[international airport]] serving [[Varanasi]], [[Uttar Pradesh]], [[India]]. It is located at [[Babatpur]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Varanasi|url=http://www.aai.aero/allAirports/varanasi_generalinfo.jsp|publisher=[[Airports Authority of India]]|access-date=1 February 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120629091735/http://www.aai.aero/allAirports/varanasi_generalinfo.jsp|archive-date=29 June 2012}}</ref> {{convert|26|km|mi|abbr=on}} northwest of Varanasi. Formerly known as Varanasi Airport, it was officially renamed after [[Lal Bahadur Shastri]], the [[List of Prime Ministers of India|2nd]] [[Prime Minister of India]], in October 2005.<ref name=pib>{{cite web|url=http://pib.nic.in/release/release.asp?relid=12805&kwd|title=Varanasi Airport renamed|publisher=Press Information Bureau, Government of India|date=20 October 2005}}</ref> It acquired its position in India's major airports after more than 4 million passengers used the airport in 2024-25.<ref name="AAI3"/> It is the [[List of the busiest airports in India|19th-busiest airport in India]] in terms of passenger movement, and the second-busiest airport in Uttar Pradesh. The airport was awarded as the best airport in [[Asia-Pacific]] in 2020 (2 to 5 million passengers per annum) by [[Airports Council International]].<ref>{{cite web |title=2020 - Best Airport by Size and Region |url=https://aci.aero/customer-experience-asq/asq-awards-and-recognition/asq-awards/current-winner-2020/best-airport-by-size-and-region/ |website=ACI World |access-date=3 March 2021}}</ref> It is the first airport in India to make announcements in [[Sanskrit language]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Varanasi International Airport makes announcement in Sanskrit |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/travel/travel-news/varanasi-international-airport-makes-announcement-in-sanskrit/articleshow/92434542.cms |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257 |date=24 June 2022 |access-date=8 June 2024}}</ref>

==Terminal==
[[file:Varanasi Airport.png|thumb|left|Lal Bahadur Shastri statue at Varanasi Airport]]
An integrated terminal serves both domestic and international flights, with a floor area of {{Convert|3900|m2|abbr=off}}.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lal Bahadur Shastri Airport or Varanasi Airport (VNS)|url=https://www.makemytrip.com/flights/varanasi_airport-vns-varanasi.html}}</ref> The terminal features 16 check-in counters with CUTE (common-user terminal equipment), four immigration counters that double up as emigration counters, and two baggage-claim belts.<ref name="auto1">{{cite web|title=Lal Bahadur Shastri Airport or Varanasi Airport (VNS)|url=https://www.aai.aero/en/node/2919|website=AAI|access-date=6 January 2021}}</ref> Besides an upper-level seating area for the aero-bridge gates, the terminal features a ground-level gate to reach other aircraft on the apron on foot, or via shuttle bus.<ref name="auto1"/> The apron can simultaneously park five narrow-body aircraft.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.goindigo.in/airport-directory/india/varanasi-vns.html|title=Varanasi Airport (VNS), Varanasi International Airport | IndiGo|website=www.goindigo.in|access-date=11 February 2020}}</ref> The waiting area features essential services for the passengers, besides snack stalls, a travellers' convenience store, a bookstore with a newsstand, and stores selling merchandise indigenous to Varanasi, such as Banarasi Saris; and a VIP waiting lounge.<ref>{{cite web|title=Shopping|url=https://www.aai.aero/en/airports/passenger-info/varanasi/Shopping|website=AAI|access-date=6 January 2021}}</ref>

[[File:Replica of varanasi ghats at varanasi airport.jpg|alt=Replica of varanasi ghats at varanasi airport|thumb|Replica of Varanasi [[ghats]] at Varanasi Airport]]

==Airfield==
The airport features a single asphalt runway bearing 09/27. It is 9,006 feet (2,745 m) in length, with turnarounds on both ends, and two exits to the main apron.<ref name="auto1"/> A third, seldom-used exit leads to an isolated apron for use in emergency.<ref name="auto1"/>
[[File:04-MAY-2023 - 6E374 CCU-VNS (A320 - VT-IAX) (05).jpg|thumb|An IndiGo aircraft being serviced by three mobile gangways at Varanasi Airport]]

==Future plans and projects==
Due to increasing passenger traffic and aircraft movements, the [[Airports Authority of India]] is planning to extend the runway to {{convert|4075|m|ft|abbr=on}} from the existing {{convert|2750|m|ft|abbr=on}}. An underpass will be constructed as the expansion will intersect with National Highway 31.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/varanasi/up-airport-1st-to-have-national-highway-under-runway/articleshow/64457458.cms|title=UP airport 1st to have national highway under runway - Times of India|website=The Times of India|date=5 June 2018 }}</ref>

In November 2019, the Airports Authority of India came up with a proposal for a new second terminal, which will be completed by 2024. The total area of the terminal will be 58,691 m<sup>2</sup> with passenger capacity of 4.5 million per year.<ref>{{cite news |title=गंगा की लहरों व शिवलिंग सा होगा वाराणसी एलबीएस इंटरनेशनल एयरपोर्ट टर्मिनल, डिजाइन तैयार |url=https://www.jagran.com/uttar-pradesh/varanasi-city-new-airport-terminal-will-be-made-as-shivling-shape-19739101.html |access-date=11 February 2020 |work=Dainik Jagran |date=10 November 2019 |language=hi}}</ref>

On 20 October 2024, Prime Minister [[Narendra Modi]] laid the foundation stone for several projects at the Airport, including the expansion of the [[airport runway]], a new [[Airport terminal|terminal]] building, and other allied works, totalling around ₹2,870 crore.<ref>{{cite news |title=PM Modi to launch several projects during his Varanasi visit |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/pm-modi-to-launch-several-projects-during-his-varanasi-visit/article68775079.ece |work=The Hindu |agency=PTI |date=20 October 2024 |access-date=21 October 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=PM Modi in Varanasi today to unveil ₹6,100 crore Diwali gift, inaugurate multiple projects |url=https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/pm-narendra-modi-uttar-pradesh-varanasi-today-projects-over-rs-6-100-cr-rj-sankara-eye-hospital-sports-complex-airport-11729386543875.html |work=Mint |date=20 October 2024 |access-date=21 October 2024}}</ref>
